plan.step: 3. Nhược điểm (tái dùng đề 66)
plan.think: Đo hẹp và bị áp lực / tiền bạc làm méo; dùng lại gần nguyên cụm và ví dụ nghệ sĩ để thấy rõ tính tái sử dụng.

plan.step: 4. Kiến nghị cân bằng
plan.think: Kết bằng cụm 'one source of evidence among several': nhận cả giá trị lẫn hạn chế.

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết giải quyết đúng đề, lập luận khá đầy đủ và mạch lạc. Tuy nhiên, một số diễn đạt chưa thật tự nhiên và độ phức tạp ngữ pháp còn dừng ở mức khá. Điểm tổng thể khoảng 7.5.
weaknesses: Một số cụm từ chưa tự nhiên, cần trau chuốt collocation.
Cấu trúc so sánh trong câu 'as much as ability' hơi elip, nên viết đầy đủ.
Phần kết luận hơi ngắn và chưa phát triển hết quan điểm cá nhân.
Đôi khi câu dài nối nhiều ý có thể gây khó theo dõi.

essays.question: What are the causes of student debt? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
The issue of student debt is a matter of growing concern. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Financial barriers play a substantial part in student debt. Rising tuition fees, living costs and the loss of income while studying discourage many people from continuing their education or push them into heavy borrowing. This is particularly true for those from modest backgrounds. In addition, social and economic disadvantage lies behind student debt in many families. Students whose parents cannot help with fees or rent have no alternative to loans, and graduates who then find only low-paid or insecure work struggle to repay them. A student from a low-income family, for example, may finish a degree owing the equivalent of several years' salary.

To address this issue, provision should be made more flexible and affordable. Grants, scholarships and subsidised accommodation reduce the amount that students need to borrow, and loans repaid only when graduates earn above a certain income protect them from unmanageable payments. Barriers fall as a result, and participation rises among groups that were previously excluded. In addition, governments should commit more funding to higher education, since this tackles the problem at its source. Extra money can be channelled into lowering fees, expanding paid work-study placements and promoting alternatives such as apprenticeships, in which learners earn while they study, so that fewer young people need to borrow at all.

In conclusion, student debt stems mainly from financial barriers and social disadvantage, but affordable provision and greater investment offer a realistic way forward.

grade.summary: Bài viết đạt chất lượng tốt, bố cục rõ ràng, lập luận chặt chẽ và ngữ pháp vững chắc. Tuy nhiên, việc phát triển sâu hơn về mặt giải pháp kinh tế vĩ mô có thể giúp bài viết đạt điểm cao hơn ở tiêu chí Task Response.
weaknesses: Phần nguyên nhân và giải pháp có sự trùng lặp nhẹ về ý tưởng (tập trung chủ yếu vào chi phí học phí và hỗ trợ tài chính).
Thiếu sự phát triển sâu hơn về mặt hệ thống giáo dục ở phần giải pháp.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết đã trả lời đầy đủ hai phần của câu hỏi (nguyên nhân và giải pháp). Lập luận rõ ràng và có đưa ra ví dụ minh họa cụ thể, đáp ứng tốt yêu cầu của đề bài.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với cấu trúc 4 đoạn chuẩn mực. Các từ nối và phương tiện liên kết được sử dụng tự nhiên và hiệu quả giữa các câu, các đoạn.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng tốt các cụm từ chuyên môn như 'financial barriers', 'modest backgrounds', 'subsidised accommodation'. Tuy nhiên, một số cụm từ chưa thực sự tạo dấu ấn ở mức band 8.0+.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, từ câu đơn đến câu phức đều được kiểm soát tốt với độ chính xác cao. Ngữ pháp không có lỗi lớn, thể hiện sự vững vàng trong việc sử dụng các thì và mệnh đề.

analysis.type_vi: Causes / Solutions: nguyên nhân và giải pháp nợ sinh viên

plan.step: 1. Khung nguyên nhân + giải pháp
plan.think: Hai nguyên nhân (rào cản tài chính, hoàn cảnh gia đình khó khăn) và hai giải pháp (học phí / hỗ trợ cả phải chăng, tăng đầu tư và lựa chọn thay thế).

plan.step: 2. Nguyên nhân
plan.think: Tái dùng ý học phí và chi phí sống (đề 270, 230) và ý hoàn cảnh gia đình (đề 149). Ví dụ sinh viên từ gia đình thu nhập thấp ra trường nợ bằng nhiều năm lương.

plan.step: 3. Giải pháp
plan.think: Học bổng, trợ cấp, khoản vay trả theo thu nhập (cụm từ đề 270); đầu tư thêm, làm thêm có hướng dẫn và học nghề vừa làm vừa học (ý đề 329).

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết ở mức khá, trả lời đúng đề và có vốn từ học thuật tốt. Để lên band cao hơn, cần phân biệt rõ các nguyên nhân, thêm ví dụ cụ thể cho giải pháp và tinh chỉnh một số collocation, cấu trúc câu.
weaknesses: Nguyên nhân 'financial barriers' và 'social disadvantage' chưa được phân biệt rạch ròi, có phần lặp ý.
Giải pháp chưa có ví dụ hoặc số liệu cụ thể nên tính thuyết phục chưa cao.
Lặp 'In addition' ở hai đoạn thân bài.
Một số cụm collocation và cấu trúc câu còn chung chung hoặc mơ hồ.

essays.question: Some argue that free university tuition increases equality. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
Some governments have abolished university tuition fees in the belief that this promotes equality. I largely agree that free tuition increases equality, since it removes a major financial barrier, although it cannot achieve equality on its own.

To begin with, free tuition opens higher education to talented students from low-income families. Where fees are high, young people from modest backgrounds may decide not to apply at all, fearing years of debt that they cannot repay, and those who do apply may choose cheaper courses regardless of their abilities. Removing fees means that ability, rather than family income, decides who studies, which strengthens social mobility. A pupil with excellent grades whose parents cannot afford to support her, for example, can accept a place without risking heavy debt.

Furthermore, free tuition benefits society by widening the pool of skilled graduates, which raises productivity and narrows the gap between rich and poor over time. However, its effect on equality has limits. Taxpayers must fund it, and some of the benefit goes to wealthier students who would have paid anyway. In addition, inequality begins long before university, in the quality of early education and in family support, so students from disadvantaged areas may still fail to reach higher education. Free tuition therefore needs to be combined with support for living costs and investment in early schooling.

In conclusion, free university tuition promotes equality to a large extent by removing a financial barrier, but real equality also requires earlier support and help with living costs.

grade.summary: Bài viết đạt chất lượng rất tốt với lập luận mạch lạc, từ vựng học thuật phù hợp và ngữ pháp chính xác. Đáp ứng hoàn hảo yêu cầu của một bài IELTS Writing Task 2 ở mức band 8.0.
weaknesses: Một số cấu trúc câu có thể được nâng cấp thêm tính học thuật để đạt điểm từ vựng cao hơn.
Phần phản biện về mặt hạn chế có thể được đào sâu hơn chút nữa.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời rất tốt câu hỏi To what extent do you agree, thể hiện rõ lập trường đồng ý phần lớn (largely agree). Các ý được phát triển logic, cân bằng giữa lợi ích của học phí miễn phí và những hạn chế của nó.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết chuẩn mực với 4 đoạn rõ ràng. Các liên từ và từ chỉ dẫn (To begin with, Furthermore, However, In conclusion) được sử dụng linh hoạt và tự nhiên.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác các cụm từ chủ đề giáo dục và tài chính như 'social mobility', 'financial barrier', 'widening the pool of skilled graduates'. Đôi chỗ từ vựng ở mức an toàn nhưng diễn đạt trôi chảy.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng từ câu đơn đến câu phức, mệnh đề quan hệ và câu điều kiện được kiểm soát tốt. Ngữ pháp chính xác gần như tuyệt đối, không có lỗi lặp cấu trúc.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: 'free university tuition increases equality' → largely agree + giới hạn

plan.step: 1. Cặp đề với 270 (học phí)
plan.think: Đề 270 nhìn từ góc 'học phí là rào cản'; đề này nhìn từ góc 'bỏ học phí giúp gì cho bình đẳng'. Dùng cùng ý nền nhưng đổi chiều lập luận, và thêm giới hạn riêng: người giàu cũng hưởng lợi, bất bình đẳng bắt đầu từ sớm.

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — mở cửa đại học cho học sinh nghèo
plan.think: Tái dùng cụm 'fearing years of debt' và 'ability rather than family income' từ đề 270; ví dụ học sinh điểm cao có thể nhận suất học.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 2 + giới hạn
plan.think: Mở rộng nguồn cử nhân, thu hẹp khoảng cách giàu nghèo. 'However': chi phí do người đóng thuế, người giàu cũng hưởng, bất bình đẳng bắt đầu từ giáo dục sớm (tái dùng ý đề 70).

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết tốt, trả lời đúng yêu cầu đề bài, lập luận mạch lạc và sử dụng ngôn ngữ học thuật khá ổn. Điểm yếu chủ yếu nằm ở một vài collocation chưa chuẩn và ví dụ minh họa chưa đủ cụ thể. Nếu trau chuốt thêm từ vựng và mở rộng ví dụ, bài có thể đạt band 8.5.
weaknesses: Một số cụm từ chưa đạt độ tự nhiên chuẩn collocation như 'opens higher education', 'risking heavy debt'.
Ví dụ minh họa còn chung chung, thiếu tính cụ thể.
Lặp lại từ 'free tuition' nhiều lần, có thể thay thế bằng các cụm đồng nghĩa.
Phần nêu giới hạn có thể được phát triển thêm để tăng chiều sâu lập luận.

essays.question: Some people say that community service should be compulsory for students. Do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Community service, such as helping in care homes or cleaning public spaces, is voluntary in most schools. I agree that it should be compulsory for students, since it builds empathy and practical skills and strengthens communities, although it should be organised flexibly.

To begin with, compulsory community service develops empathy and a sense of responsibility. Pupils who spend time with elderly residents, homeless people or children with disabilities see problems that they would rarely meet in their own neighbourhoods, and this experience makes social issues real rather than abstract. They also learn teamwork, communication and reliability, qualities valued by employers and universities. A teenager who helps to run a weekly food bank, for example, learns how much effort is needed to support people in need.

Furthermore, communities benefit from the extra help. Schools that require a modest number of service hours each year provide charities, hospitals and local authorities with willing volunteers, and many projects, such as environmental clean-ups, would not happen otherwise. Some argue that compulsion undermines genuine goodwill, since students may resent being forced. However, many pupils who begin reluctantly continue voluntarily once they see the results, and a requirement ensures that all students, not only the already motivated, gain the experience. Schools can minimise resentment by letting pupils choose from a range of projects that match their interests and timetables, so that service feels like an opportunity rather than a punishment.

In conclusion, I believe that community service should be compulsory because it benefits both students and society, provided that pupils are given a genuine choice of activities.

grade.summary: Bài viết đạt chất lượng tốt với lập luận rõ ràng, cấu trúc mạch lạc và từ ngữ phong phú. Học viên đã trả lời trọn vẹn yêu cầu đề bài theo đúng định hướng Agree/Disagree ở mức band điểm khá cao.
weaknesses: Một số ví dụ còn hơi chung chung, có thể cụ thể hóa hơn nữa.
Cách dùng từ đôi chỗ còn lặp lại ý tưởng về lợi ích của học sinh.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi thảo luận, nêu rõ quan điểm đồng tình ngay từ mở bài và phát triển các luận điểm chặt chẽ. Các khía cạnh về lợi ích cho học sinh và xã hội được phân tích kỹ lưỡng, đồng thời có cân nhắc góc nhìn đối lập (counter-argument).
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với các đoạn văn rõ ràng, sử dụng các từ nối hiệu quả (To begin with, Furthermore, However, In conclusion). Các ý tưởng được triển khai logic từ khái quát đến chi tiết có ví dụ minh họa.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác nhiều cụm từ tốt (empathy and a sense of responsibility, social issues, genuine goodwill). Tuy nhiên, một số cụm từ còn khá thông thường và có thể nâng cấp thêm độ tự nhiên.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc ngữ pháp đa dạng, kết hợp linh hoạt câu đơn và câu phức với các mệnh đề quan hệ và trạng ngữ chỉ thời gian. Đội ngũ kiểm tra ghi nhận độ chính xác cao, ít lỗi ngữ pháp.

analysis.type_vi: Agree / Disagree: 'community service should be compulsory for students' → đồng ý có điều kiện

plan.step: 1. Chọn phe và dự đoán phản bác
plan.think: Phản bác chính là 'ép buộc làm mất thiện chí'. Đưa phản bác này vào thân bài 2 kèm giải pháp (cho học sinh tự chọn dự án).

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — đồng cảm và kỹ năng
plan.think: Tiếp xúc người già, người vô gia cư, trẻ khuyết tật làm vấn đề xã hội thành thật; học làm việc nhóm, giao tiếp, đáng tin. Ví dụ ngân hàng thực phẩm.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 2 — lợi ích cho cộng đồng + phản bác
plan.think: Tổ chức từ thiện, bệnh viện có thêm nhân lực; nhiều em bắt đầu miễn cưỡng nhưng sau tự nguyện tiếp tục. Giải pháp: cho chọn dự án để bớt bức bách.

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết đạt mức band 8 nếu khắc phục một số cụm từ chưa tự nhiên. Lập luận chặt chẽ, phát triển ý tốt, nhưng cần chú ý diễn đạt collocation chính xác hơn và tinh gọn phần mở bài.
weaknesses: Một vài collocation chưa tự nhiên ('meet problems', 'the already motivated').
Mở bài hơi dài và nhồi nhét ý điều kiện, làm giảm sự rõ ràng ban đầu.
Thiếu câu chuyển ý giữa hai đoạn thân bài để tăng độ mạch lạc.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that standardized tests are fair?

versions.text:
Standardised tests are often defended as the fairest way of judging students because everyone answers identical questions. I disagree with this view, since equal questions do not guarantee equal conditions, and a single test captures too little of what students can do.

To begin with, students do not arrive at the test on equal terms. Pupils whose families can afford private tutors, practice papers and quiet study spaces enjoy a clear advantage over equally able classmates who cannot, so a high score may reflect household income as much as ability. Language and cultural background also matter: a question framed around an unfamiliar situation can confuse students from different communities even when they know the underlying content. Consequently, a procedure that looks neutral can quietly reinforce existing inequalities. A talented pupil who studies in a crowded home and learns English as a second language, for example, may be unable to show her true level.

Furthermore, a single test offers only a snapshot of performance on one day. Illness, nerves or a family problem can lower the result of even a very capable candidate, while the format rewards memory and speed under timed conditions and ignores creativity, teamwork and practical skills. Admittedly, standardised tests are easy to compare, but being easy to compare is not the same as being fair. Assessment that combines coursework, projects and classroom observation over a longer period would give a more complete and just picture.

In conclusion, I cannot accept that standardised tests are fair, because unequal preparation and a narrow, one-day snapshot distort the results.

grade.summary: Bài viết đạt chất lượng tốt, có lập luận sắc bén, bố cục mạch lạc và vốn từ vựng phong phú. Người viết đã thành công trong việc chứng minh tại sao các bài kiểm tra chuẩn hóa không công bằng thông qua các luận điểm về điều kiện xuất thân và hạn chế của một bài kiểm tra đơn lẻ.

Độ dài vừa đủ vượt mức tối thiểu một chút, có thể mở rộng thêm một vài khía cạnh nhỏ nếu muốn.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời trực tiếp câu hỏi đề bài và duy trì lập trường không đồng tình xuyên suốt. Các luận điểm được phát triển tốt với ví dụ cụ thể, đáp ứng đầy đủ yêu cầu của một bài viết IELTS Writing Task 2.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bài viết có bố cục rõ ràng với phần mở đầu, thân bài và kết luận mạch lạc. Các từ nối và phương tiện liên kết được sử dụng tự nhiên, giúp người đọc dễ dàng theo dõi mạch suy nghĩ.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, tự nhiên và phù hợp với chủ đề giáo dục. Người viết sử dụng thành công một số cụm từ hay (collocations) như 'household income', 'underlying content', 'snapshot of performance'.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, từ câu đơn đến câu phức, được sử dụng chính xác hầu như tuyệt đối. Ngữ pháp và các thì trong bài được kiểm soát rất tốt, không có lỗi cấu trúc lớn.

analysis.type_vi: Agree / Disagree: 'standardized tests are fair' → phản đối (khác đề 66 ở trọng tâm: công bằng chứ không phải chính xác)

plan.step: 1. Đọc đúng từ khoá 'fair'
plan.think: Đề 66 hỏi 'accurately measure', đề này hỏi 'fair'. Vì vậy lý do 1 phải nói về điều kiện không bình đẳng (tiền, ngôn ngữ, văn hoá), lý do 2 về tính một lần và chỉ đo hẹp, và câu nhượng bộ dùng 'not the same as being fair'.

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — điều kiện khác nhau

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết trả lời đúng yêu cầu đề bài, lập trường phản đối rõ ràng và được hỗ trợ bởi hai luận điểm thuyết phục kèm ví dụ thực tế. Ngôn ngữ mạch lạc, từ vựng học thuật tốt, chỉ cần chỉnh lại một vài collocation và diễn đạt nhỏ để đạt mức tự nhiên hơn. Tổng thể bài đạt khoảng band 8.0.

essays.question: Some believe that religious education should be part of the school curriculum. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Debates about religion in schools often divide families and politicians. I largely agree that religious education should be part of the curriculum, provided that it teaches about many beliefs in a balanced way rather than instructing pupils in a single faith.

To begin with, learning about religions builds cultural understanding. Religious ideas shape art, literature, law and politics in countries around the world, so pupils who know the basics of major faiths understand history and current events far better. In diverse societies, familiarity with different beliefs also weakens prejudice, since people are less likely to rely on stereotypes about those they understand. Pupils also gain the vocabulary to discuss sensitive subjects calmly and respectfully. A class that studies how festivals such as Diwali, Ramadan and Christmas are celebrated, for example, learns respect for neighbours' traditions.

However, religious education has legitimate limits. Beliefs are a private matter, and parents differ widely in what they wish their children to be taught, so a lesson that promotes one faith may clash with family wishes and amount to indoctrination. It also risks overloading a timetable that is already full, which could reduce time for core subjects such as literacy and science. Schools should therefore teach about religions factually and neutrally, alongside non-religious worldviews, and allow families to choose whether their children take part in devotional activities. Such an approach protects freedom of belief while still giving all pupils the knowledge they need to live peacefully with others.

In conclusion, religious education deserves a place in the curriculum to a large extent, as a neutral study of beliefs that promotes understanding, but it should never become religious instruction.

grade.summary: Bài viết đạt chất lượng tốt với tư duy phản biện sắc sảo, lập luận chặt chẽ và văn phong học thuật phù hợp. Việc định hình rõ ràng ranh giới giữa việc 'học về tôn giáo' và 'truyền bá tôn giáo' giúp bài viết ghi điểm cao.

Một số câu ghép có cấu trúc tương đối dài, đôi khi có thể ngắt nhỏ để tăng tính rõ ràng.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi theo hướng đồng ý một phần (largely agree) với các điều kiện cụ thể. Lập luận rõ ràng, sắc sảo và bao quát được cả mặt lợi lẫn mặt hạn chế của vấn đề.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc, chia đoạn hợp lý với câu chủ đề rõ ràng ở mỗi đoạn thân bài. Các từ nối và phương tiện liên kết được sử dụng tự nhiên và hiệu quả.
feedback.lexicalResource: Từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác các thuật ngữ liên quan đến giáo dục và tôn giáo như 'indoctrination', 'devotional activities', 'worldviews'. Lỗi chính tả không có.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc ngữ pháp đa dạng, từ câu phức đến câu ghép đều được kiểm soát tốt. Các thì và sự hòa hợp chủ ngữ - động từ được sử dụng chính xác.

plan.step: 1. Tách 'dạy VỀ tôn giáo' khỏi 'dạy THEO một tôn giáo'
plan.think: Đây là chìa khoá để trả lời đề 'extent': đồng ý với phần đầu, phản đối phần sau. Toàn bài bám vào sự phân biệt này.

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — hiểu văn hoá, giảm định kiến
plan.think: Tôn giáo định hình nghệ thuật, văn học, luật pháp, chính trị. Tái dùng cụm weaken prejudice và ý tôn trọng truyền thống người khác (đề 103). Ví dụ lễ hội Diwali, Ramadan, Giáng sinh.

essays.question: Many people say that studying arts improves academic performance. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Some people claim that studying the arts raises academic performance. I largely agree, since artistic activities develop concentration and motivation that carry over into other subjects, although the arts are not a substitute for core teaching.

To begin with, arts subjects train skills that support academic study. Learning to draw, act or play an instrument demands careful observation, sustained concentration and patient, repeated effort, and these habits carry over into mathematics, science and writing. Research has associated musical and visual training with stronger memory and spatial reasoning, which helps pupils to understand diagrams and solve problems. A pupil who has spent months mastering a difficult piece, for example, learns that perseverance eventually produces results, and may approach a hard mathematics problem with greater determination.

Furthermore, the arts keep many pupils engaged with school. Students who find written exams discouraging often thrive when they can perform, design or create something tangible, and this success restores their confidence and improves attendance and effort in other lessons. Pupils who feel that school values their strengths are also less likely to drop out. However, the evidence is not entirely clear. Better results may partly reflect the fact that motivated or well-supported pupils choose the arts, and arts classes cannot replace direct teaching of literacy and numeracy. Their value lies in complementing, not replacing, core lessons within a balanced timetable, and schools should therefore measure the effects carefully before making large changes.

In conclusion, I largely agree that studying the arts improves academic performance by building concentration, perseverance and engagement, although their benefits depend on a balanced curriculum.

grade.summary: Bài viết của bạn có chất lượng tốt, cấu trúc rõ ràng và tư duy lập luận logic ở mức band 7.5. Để đạt điểm cao hơn, cần tinh chỉnh cách sắp xếp ý kiến phản biện để tập trung hoàn toàn vào lập trường chính.

plan.step: 1. Cẩn trọng với từ 'improves'
plan.think: Đây là khẳng định nhân quả nên cần thừa nhận có thể chỉ là tương quan (học sinh có động lực chọn nghệ thuật). Nêu giới hạn đó ở thân bài 2 làm bài trung thực hơn và an toàn khi bị chấm Task Response.

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — kỹ năng chuyển giao (tái dùng đề 114)

essays.question: Some argue that tuition fees limit access to higher education. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
As tuition fees rise in many countries, some people argue that they prevent talented students from attending university. I largely agree, since fees discourage young people from low-income families and burden others with debt, although they are not the only barrier.

To begin with, high fees place a heavy financial burden on students and their families. Tuition, accommodation and living expenses can consume a family's savings, and young people from modest backgrounds may decide not to apply at all, fearing years of debt that they cannot repay. Others choose cheaper courses or universities near home, regardless of their talents. As a result, ability alone does not decide who studies, and society loses the potential of capable students. A pupil with excellent grades whose parents cannot afford to support her, for example, may give up her place or choose a different path.

Furthermore, restricted access widens inequality. Where higher education is a privilege reserved for wealthy families, graduates are drawn disproportionately from the same social groups, which reduces social mobility and weakens the economy's supply of skilled workers. However, fees are not the only obstacle. Poor school results, lack of information and low expectations also keep some students out, and universities need funding from somewhere. Governments can reduce the barrier by offering grants, scholarships and loans repaid only when graduates earn above a certain income, so that cost is not the deciding factor for capable students.

In conclusion, I agree to a large extent that tuition fees limit access to higher education, but access can be protected through well-designed financial support.

Tuy nhiên, việc đề cập đến các rào cản khác và giải pháp ở phần thân bài thứ hai làm cho cấu trúc tranh luận có phần hơi lan man nhưng vẫn chấp nhận được.

feedback.lexicalResource: Sử dụng từ vựng phong phú và phù hợp với chủ đề giáo dục như 'financial burden', 'modest backgrounds', 'social mobility', và 'disproportionately'. Hầu hết các cụm từ được dùng chính xác, tự nhiên.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on policing or on education? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Opinions differ as to whether public money is better spent on policing or on education. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, those who favour policing argue that public safety is the foundation of everyday life. Residents who feel secure are more likely to work, invest and send their children to school, whereas high crime discourages business and drives people away. Visible, well-resourced policing can deter offences before they occur and shorten emergency response times, which may save lives. Police presence also reassures vulnerable groups such as elderly residents and shopkeepers. A neighbourhood with regular patrols, for instance, tends to experience fewer break-ins.

On the other hand, supporters of education point out that it tackles the root causes of crime. Educated individuals are statistically more inclined to find stable employment and less prone to criminal behaviour, which eases the burden on police, courts and prisons. Quality schooling also gives young people from deprived areas alternatives to gangs and illegal work. Educated citizens also vote, pay taxes and take part in community life. In the long term, therefore, spending on schools reduces the need to spend on enforcement. A community in which most residents have completed secondary school, for example, typically reports lower crime and healthier habits.

To sum up, both positions have their merits; nevertheless, I believe that education should take priority, because it tackles the root causes of crime instead of merely responding to its consequences, while basic policing must still be adequately funded.

essays.question: Some believe that standardized uniforms improve student equality. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Some educators argue that requiring all pupils to wear the same uniform promotes equality among students. I largely agree, since uniforms hide visible differences in family wealth and reduce the pressure to compete over clothing, but they cannot remove deeper inequalities.

To begin with, a common uniform masks differences in income that would otherwise be obvious. Without it, pupils from wealthy families can arrive in expensive branded clothes, while those from low-income households may feel embarrassed by worn or secondhand items, and this contrast is a frequent cause of teasing and bullying. When everyone dresses the same, children are judged by their behaviour and effort rather than by labels. A pupil who cannot afford fashionable trainers, for example, no longer stands out as different.

Furthermore, uniforms ease the financial burden on families. Parents no longer face constant demands for the latest fashion, and a few durable items cost less than a wardrobe of everyday clothes, so households with limited budgets are spared an unfair expense. Pupils also gain a stronger sense of belonging, which supports cooperation across social groups. Nevertheless, uniforms have limits. Good-quality uniforms can themselves be expensive, and equality in appearance does not remove inequality in resources, home support or opportunity. They should therefore be affordable and supported by subsidies for poorer families.

In conclusion, I believe that uniforms promote equality to a large extent by concealing wealth and reducing competition, although genuine equality also requires fair funding and support.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on technological education? Use examples.

versions.text:
Technological skills are becoming indispensable in almost every profession. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on technological education: a workforce suited to the modern economy and a stronger capacity for innovation.

First and foremost, technological education prepares young people for a world in which software underpins almost every industry. Finance, healthcare, design and even farming now rely on programs that analyse data and automate routine tasks, so employees who understand how such tools work have a clear advantage. As a result, businesses recruit qualified staff more easily, productivity rises and fewer workers are left behind when jobs are automated. Even pupils who never become engineers will be better able to use, question and adapt the technology that shapes their working lives. An accountant who can write a short script to process thousands of invoices, for example, finishes in minutes what once took days.

In addition, a strong technological education system promotes innovation and competitiveness. Educated citizens are more likely to start companies and develop new technologies, which creates jobs and attracts investment, and countries with a deep pool of engineers and programmers can compete in industries such as software, medicine and clean energy. Graduates in technology also help the public sector to improve services, from transport to healthcare. Singapore, a small country with few natural resources, is often cited as a nation that built its prosperity chiefly on the quality of its schools and universities. Because technology changes quickly, a country that teaches adaptable problem-solving skills, not just current tools, is better placed to keep pace.

To sum up, technological education brings clear benefits to a country, above all a workforce suited to modern industry and a stronger capacity for innovation. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

essays.question: Some people say that homework improves learning outcomes. Do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Many parents and teachers assume that the more homework pupils do, the better they will learn. I disagree with this view, since extra work at home often brings little academic gain while taking a heavy toll on children's wellbeing and widening the gap between families.

To begin with, more homework does not necessarily mean more learning. Beyond a modest amount, additional tasks tend to produce diminishing returns, particularly for younger pupils, because repetitive worksheets and copied answers consume time without deepening understanding. Exhausted children also absorb less in the following day's lessons, which defeats the purpose of the extra work. Resentment builds, and some pupils come to associate learning with chores rather than curiosity. A child who spends two hours copying definitions every evening, for example, rarely gains more understanding than one who completes a single well-designed task.

Furthermore, homework often benefits the pupils who need it least. At home, children from crowded or noisy households, or with parents who cannot explain difficult tasks, are at a clear disadvantage compared with classmates who have a quiet desk and a private tutor, so assignments frequently measure family circumstances rather than ability. Some argue that homework teaches self-discipline, but this skill can equally be developed through supervised independent study during the school day. Learning that takes place in class gives everyone the same conditions and the same support, and teachers see what each pupil can do unaided.

In conclusion, I do not believe that homework improves learning outcomes in any meaningful way, given its diminishing returns and its unfair effects on disadvantaged pupils.

analysis.type_vi: Agree / Disagree: 'homework improves learning outcomes' → phản đối (khác đề 46: trọng tâm là HIỆU QUẢ học tập)

essays.question: Discuss the role of physical education in schools.

versions.text:
Physical education is sometimes dismissed as a break from real lessons, yet it plays a valuable part in schooling. This essay will outline two important roles: protecting children's health and supporting their wellbeing and learning.

First and foremost, physical education promotes health and active habits. Many children now spend hours sitting at desks and screens, and rates of obesity and related illness are rising in many countries. Regular, well-taught PE keeps pupils active, builds strength and coordination, and teaches them how exercise and nutrition affect the body. Habits formed in childhood often last into adulthood, so schools are well placed to reduce long-term health problems and the pressure they place on health services. A child who learns to enjoy swimming or running at school, for example, is more likely to remain active as an adult.

In addition, PE supports mental wellbeing, social skills and concentration. Exercise helps young people to relieve stress and improve their mood, and pupils who move regularly tend to concentrate better in later lessons. Team games also teach cooperation, fair play and shared responsibility, qualities that classroom lessons alone rarely instil. Moreover, success in sport can build self-confidence, particularly for pupils who struggle academically. A shy pupil who gains confidence by scoring in a team game, for example, may speak up more readily in other lessons.

To sum up, physical education plays a vital role by protecting health and by nurturing wellbeing and teamwork. For these reasons, it deserves a secure place in every school timetable.

essays.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using social media for education.

versions.text:
Platforms such as Facebook, YouTube and WhatsApp are now part of students' daily lives, and many teachers have begun to use them for learning. This essay will discuss the main advantages and disadvantages of this trend.

On the positive side, social media makes collaboration and access to resources easier. Students can create study groups, share notes and ask questions outside class hours, while teachers can post explanations or video lessons that pupils watch at their own pace. Because these platforms are already familiar, learners often engage with them more readily than with formal systems, and communication feels quick and informal. During school closures, for example, many classes continued through messaging groups when other tools were unavailable.

On the negative side, social media carries the risk of distraction and misinformation. Notifications, games and entertaining videos offer endless temptations, so a student who opens a study group may end up scrolling for an hour. In addition, false claims often spread faster than corrections, and pupils who cannot check sources or spot bias may be misled. Privacy and cyberbullying are further concerns, since personal details and comments are visible to a wide audience. Without clear rules, these problems can outweigh the educational benefits.

In conclusion, social media can strengthen collaboration and widen access to learning materials, but its distractions and risks are serious. On balance, I believe that it should be used in education only in moderation, with clear guidelines, teacher supervision and lessons in evaluating information.

essays.question: To what extent should schools teach crime prevention and civic responsibility? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
Crime and social conflict affect communities everywhere, and some people argue that schools can help to prevent them. I largely agree that schools should teach crime prevention and civic responsibility, since early education is more effective than punishment and builds citizens who contribute to society, although the approach must be age-appropriate.

To begin with, teaching young people about the consequences of crime helps to prevent it. Lessons on topics such as peer pressure, drug misuse, online fraud and cyberbullying give pupils the knowledge and confidence to resist risky situations, and talks by police officers or former offenders can make the consequences vivid. Prevention is also far cheaper than dealing with offences after they occur, since each young person who avoids crime saves public money on policing and prisons. A teenager who has learned how online scams work, for example, is far less likely to become a victim or an accomplice.

Furthermore, civic education develops responsible citizens. Pupils who learn how local government works, why voting matters and how to volunteer are more likely to take part in community life as adults, and activities such as clean-up days or school councils give them practical experience of shared responsibility. Educated individuals are statistically more inclined to avoid criminal behaviour, which ultimately yields safer communities. However, lessons should be age-appropriate and avoid frightening young children, and schools cannot replace families or social services. They should therefore form one part of a wider strategy rather than the whole solution.

In conclusion, I believe that schools should teach crime prevention and civic responsibility to a large extent because prevention is effective and affordable, as long as lessons are realistic and part of a wider approach.

essays.question: Should individuals be responsible for education, or should society/government take action? Discuss.

versions.text:
People disagree about who should bear responsibility for education: individuals and their families, or society through the government. This essay will consider both views before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of individual responsibility argue that learning depends first on personal effort. Pupils who take ownership of their studies, and parents who encourage good habits at home, achieve better results than those who wait for the state to provide everything. Adults also gain from choosing and, where possible, paying for the training that suits their goals, because they value what they have invested in. Moreover, extensive state involvement can intrude on matters that arguably belong to the family, such as values and the choice of school. A family with strong religious convictions, for instance, may object to a standardised lesson on the subject.

On the other hand, advocates of government action point out that education is a public good that markets and families cannot provide equally. Without public funding, good-quality learning becomes a privilege reserved for wealthy families, leaving talented children from disadvantaged backgrounds with limited prospects. The state can also set common standards, train teachers and build schools at a scale that individuals cannot match, and society as a whole benefits from a skilled, informed population. Finland, which offers free education and consistently achieves strong results, illustrates how equal access can benefit society as a whole.

To sum up, both positions have their merits; nevertheless, I believe that the state should bear primary responsibility, with families and individuals playing a complementary role.

essays.question: To what extent should financial literacy be taught in schools? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
Many young adults leave school able to solve equations but unsure how to budget, save or borrow wisely. I largely agree that financial literacy should be taught in schools, since it protects young people from costly mistakes and builds habits that benefit them for life, provided that it is integrated sensibly into existing lessons.

To begin with, understanding money helps people to avoid debt and exploitation. Credit cards, student loans, mobile payment apps and online lending all make borrowing easy, but the interest, fees and long-term consequences are often hard to understand. Pupils who learn how interest works and how to compare offers are less likely to be misled by aggressive advertising or to fall into unmanageable debt. A graduate who understands compound interest, for example, will think carefully before relying on a credit card to cover everyday expenses.

Furthermore, early lessons in budgeting and saving shape lifelong habits. Children who practise planning a monthly budget, setting savings goals and distinguishing needs from wants are more likely to build financial security as adults, which reduces stress and lessens dependence on welfare. Financial confidence also supports wider goals such as buying a home or starting a business. However, schools need not create a new subject: the skill is best developed within existing lessons such as mathematics and citizenship, using realistic examples, so that the timetable is not overloaded. Teachers should also receive proper training, as poorly taught lessons may create false confidence rather than genuine understanding.

In conclusion, I believe that financial literacy deserves a place in the curriculum because it helps pupils avoid debt and build secure futures, provided that it is woven into existing subjects.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on public libraries or on digital resources? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether public money should support libraries or digital resources. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of libraries emphasise their role in providing free and equal access to knowledge. Books, newspapers and databases that would cost a great deal to buy individually are available free of charge, while public computers and internet connections serve residents who have none at home. Libraries also act as community hubs, offering quiet study spaces, children's story sessions and language classes for newcomers, so they nurture a reading habit from an early age. For many isolated residents, such as retired people living alone, a weekly book club may be their main source of company.

On the other hand, advocates of digital resources point out that they reach far more people at a lower cost per user. A single online database or e-book collection can serve thousands of users at once, at any hour and from any location, which is particularly valuable for rural residents, people with disabilities and working adults. Digital materials can also be updated instantly and searched in seconds, so they remain current, whereas printed books require space, storage and replacement. Platforms such as Coursera and Khan Academy, for example, now give millions of users access to everything from school mathematics to university-level courses, often free of charge.

To sum up, both positions have their merits; nevertheless, I believe that digital resources deserve priority because they reach more people at lower cost, although libraries should be modernised so that they can offer both.

essays.question: How far do you think personalized learning will change schooling in the next 20 years? Support your answer with reasons.

versions.text:
Adaptive software, online platforms and data analysis are already beginning to tailor lessons to individual pupils. I believe that personalised learning will change schooling to a large extent over the next two decades, although teachers will remain at its centre.

First and foremost, technology is making it practical to adapt teaching to each learner. In a crowded classroom, a teacher rarely has time to adjust the pace for every pupil, whereas adaptive software can identify a student's weaknesses and provide targeted practice at once. As costs fall and the software improves, such tools are likely to become standard in most schools, so that pupils progress according to understanding rather than age or class schedule. A pupil who repeatedly makes the same grammatical error, for instance, can receive tailored exercises the same day instead of waiting weeks for feedback.

In addition, personalised learning will reshape the role of teachers and the structure of lessons. Freed from repetitive marking, teachers will be able to devote more attention to discussion, mentoring and pupils who need extra support, and assessment will increasingly track progress continuously instead of relying on a single final examination. However, change will be limited by cost, data privacy and the need for human guidance. Schools in poorer regions may lack devices and connectivity, and young children still need the encouragement and social interaction that only people provide. Technology will therefore reshape schooling without replacing its human core.

In conclusion, personalised learning is likely to transform how pupils progress and how teachers spend their time, but its impact will depend on investment and on keeping teachers at the heart of education.

essays.question: Discuss the role of school counsellors in student wellbeing.

versions.text:
School counsellors are an increasingly familiar presence in modern schools. This essay will outline two roles that they play in student wellbeing: providing early emotional support, and giving guidance on learning and relationships.

First and foremost, counsellors provide early support for emotional and mental health. Pupils face pressure from exams, social media and family problems, and constant deadlines, comparison with classmates and fear of failure often lead to anxiety, sleepless nights and, in severe cases, burnout. A trained counsellor can notice warning signs, offer a confidential space to talk and refer serious cases to specialists before problems escalate. As a result, fewer students drop out or suffer long-term harm. A teenager who is anxious about exams, for example, can learn coping strategies instead of struggling alone.

In addition, counsellors give practical guidance on study, careers and relationships. They help pupils to choose subjects, plan for university or work, and develop habits such as time management. They also mediate conflicts and support victims of bullying, which creates a safer atmosphere where students can concentrate on learning. Teachers, who are not trained for these tasks, are then free to focus on teaching. Admittedly, employing counsellors costs money, and one counsellor in a large school may be overstretched. Even so, prevention is far cheaper than dealing with crises later, so schools should treat counselling as an essential service.

To sum up, school counsellors play a vital role in student wellbeing by offering early emotional support and practical guidance. For these reasons, they deserve a secure place in every school.

grade.summary: Bài viết có chất lượng tốt, lập luận chặt chẽ và bố cục rõ ràng giúp làm nổi bật vai trò của tư vấn viên học đường. Ngôn ngữ tự nhiên và ngữ pháp vững chắc là điểm mạnh lớn của bài.

essays.question: Many people say that apprenticeships provide better job prospects. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Many people say that apprenticeships give young people better job prospects than purely academic routes. I largely agree with this view, since apprentices gain practical experience, earn while they learn and are often offered permanent jobs, although the advantage depends on the field.

To begin with, apprenticeships combine paid work with training, so young people gain exactly the experience that employers look for. Instead of finishing a course with a qualification but no work history, apprentices spend several years in a real workplace, learning from experienced colleagues and building a record of reliable performance. Employers who have trained an apprentice know their strengths and often offer them a permanent post, which means the move from education to work is smooth. A teenager who learns basic electrical installation as an apprentice, for example, may qualify for a stable, well-paid position instead of drifting between short-term jobs.

Furthermore, apprenticeships avoid the debt that many graduates carry. Apprentices receive a wage and usually pay no tuition fees, so they can begin saving, renting a home and supporting themselves earlier than classmates who spend years at university. Countries with strong apprenticeship systems, such as Germany, tend to have low youth unemployment, which suggests that this route improves prospects. However, the advantage is not universal. Some professions, such as medicine and law, require full degrees, and training that is too narrow may leave workers vulnerable if technology changes their trade. The best programmes therefore include transferable skills such as communication and problem solving.

In conclusion, apprenticeships generally offer better job prospects in many fields because of practical experience, earnings and employer links, although academic routes remain essential for some careers.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on arts education or on science education? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether governments should spend more on science education or on arts education. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of science education argue that it drives economic progress and solves practical problems. Employers in sectors such as engineering, healthcare and technology increasingly seek graduates with advanced technical knowledge, digital literacy and sound problem-solving abilities, and scientific research produces the innovations that create new industries and jobs. Countries that expanded access to schooling after the Second World War, such as South Korea, later enjoyed rapid economic growth. Science education also helps citizens to understand issues such as climate change and public health, so that they can judge evidence for themselves.

On the other hand, advocates of arts education point out that it develops creativity and wellbeing that science alone cannot. Designing, composing or painting has no single correct answer, so pupils learn to generate ideas, test them and improve their work, habits that innovation itself depends on. Creating something also gives young people a healthy way to express feelings and relieve stress, and some pupils who struggle with academic subjects discover talents and confidence through art. A pupil who sees a painting displayed in the school corridor, for instance, may gain a confidence that spreads to other lessons.

To sum up, both positions have their merits; nevertheless, I believe that science should take priority because of its economic and practical value, although the arts should not be neglected.

essays.question: How far do you think remote learning will remain common after the pandemic? Support your answer with reasons.

versions.text:
Remote learning expanded dramatically during the pandemic, and many people now wonder whether it will survive the return to normal life. I believe that it will remain common to a considerable extent, mainly as part of a blended approach, because it is flexible and cost-effective but cannot replace classroom teaching for everyone.

To begin with, schools, universities and families have invested in the platforms, devices and skills needed for online study, and the experience has shown how much convenience it offers. Students can attend lessons from any location, replay recorded explanations and study around jobs or family responsibilities, which is particularly valuable for adults and for people who live far from a campus. Institutions also save on buildings and staff, so many will keep online options to reach more learners at lower cost. A university that can enrol part-time students from other regions without building new lecture halls, for example, has a strong reason to keep its online courses.

Furthermore, employers and learners increasingly value flexibility, which makes remote study a natural fit with modern working patterns. Short online courses allow professionals to update their skills without leaving their jobs. However, the extent of remote learning will be limited. Young children need the supervision, discipline and social contact of a classroom, practical subjects such as chemistry or nursing require laboratories and equipment, and families without reliable internet cannot benefit equally. These limits mean that remote learning will supplement face-to-face teaching rather than dominate it.

In conclusion, remote learning will remain common as a flexible complement to classrooms, but face-to-face teaching will continue to be essential, especially for younger and practical learners.

essays.question: How can governments promote STEM careers among girls? Suggest practical measures.

versions.text:
Women remain under-represented in science and technology careers in most countries. This essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take, focusing on role models and early exposure, and on financial and workplace support.

To begin with, awareness campaigns and visible role models would change attitudes towards the subjects. Media campaigns, mentoring by successful women scientists and engineers, and visits to laboratories and technology companies show girls that study leads to rewarding careers. Once these links become clear, motivation tends to follow. Equally important, early exposure through school clubs and hands-on projects, such as coding or robotics, builds confidence before stereotypes take hold, particularly if teachers are trained to encourage all pupils equally. A girl who builds a simple robot at primary school, for example, is more likely to see engineering as a future option.

In addition, authorities should offer attractive incentives such as scholarships and structured career pathways. Grants for girls who study science at university, internships in industry and clear routes to promotion encourage talented individuals to enter and remain in the field. Employers also need to provide flexible working hours and tackle discrimination, since young women will not choose careers in which they expect to feel unwelcome. Stronger support systems, such as mentoring schemes, would reduce the strain on those who are often the only woman in a team. A stable, supportive environment in turn raises standards for everyone and keeps skilled people in the profession.

In conclusion, role models, early exposure and financial and workplace support offer the most realistic way forward in encouraging girls to pursue careers in science and technology.

grade.summary: Bài viết hoàn thành xuất sắc yêu cầu của đề bài với tư duy logic tốt, cấu trúc rõ ràng và từ vựng phong phú. Người viết đưa ra được các giải pháp khả thi và có chiều sâu cho vấn đề khuyến khích nữ giới theo đuổi ngành STEM.

essays.question: Discuss the role of apprenticeship programs in reducing youth unemployment.

versions.text:
Youth unemployment remains a stubborn problem in many countries. This essay will outline two ways in which apprenticeship programmes help to reduce it: by giving young people the work experience that employers want and by matching training to real jobs.

First and foremost, apprenticeships solve the problem of inexperience. Many young people cannot find work because employers want experience, yet they cannot gain experience without a job. Apprenticeships break this circle by combining paid employment with training, so participants build practical skills, a record of reliable performance and professional contacts while still learning. As a result, they become attractive to employers who would otherwise reject them. A school leaver who completes a three-year apprenticeship in a hospital kitchen, for example, may be offered a permanent position at the end of it.

In addition, apprenticeships match training to the real needs of employers. Because companies help to design the programmes, young people learn the competencies that the labour market actually demands, and businesses can fill shortages of skilled workers in sectors such as construction, healthcare and engineering. Employers also benefit from a reliable supply of loyal, well-trained staff, so they have an incentive to invest. Countries with strong apprenticeship systems, such as Germany, tend to have low youth unemployment, which suggests that these programmes work. Governments pay less in welfare and gain more in tax when young people are in work, so the programmes also help public finances.

To sum up, apprenticeship programmes reduce youth unemployment by providing experience and by linking training to employers' needs. For these reasons, they deserve continued public support.

essays.question: How far do you think micro-credentials will change higher education in the next 20 years? Support your answer with reasons.

versions.text:
Micro-credentials, short and focused certificates that prove a specific skill, have grown quickly alongside online platforms. I believe that they will change higher education considerably over the next two decades, although traditional degrees will not disappear.

First and foremost, micro-credentials fit a labour market in which skills change rapidly. Technological change means that few people can rely on a single set of skills for an entire career, so workers need to update their knowledge regularly. A short course in data analysis or project management is quicker and cheaper than a full degree, and employers can see exactly what it certifies. Universities that offer such courses will attract working adults who cannot spend three years on campus. A marketing assistant who completes a short course in data analytics, for example, may qualify for a promotion within months.

In addition, micro-credentials will make higher education more flexible and personalised. Learners will be able to combine short courses from different institutions into a tailored programme, gradually building towards a recognised qualification, and this will push universities to compete on quality and relevance. However, several factors will limit the change. Regulated professions such as medicine and law will still require full degrees, and a degree provides broad analytical training that a collection of short courses may not. Employers also need to trust the quality of each credential. Micro-credentials will therefore supplement degrees rather than replace them.

In conclusion, micro-credentials are likely to reshape higher education by promoting flexible, continuous learning, but degrees will remain important for professions and for broad academic development.

essays.question: To what extent should students be involved in school governance? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
School decisions about rules, facilities and activities have traditionally been made by adults alone. I largely agree that students should be involved in governing their schools, since it develops responsibility and democratic skills, although they should not control every decision.

To begin with, taking part in decision-making teaches responsibility and democratic skills. Pupils who sit on school councils learn to listen to different views, negotiate compromises and take responsibility for the results, abilities that are valuable in work and in civic life. They also understand how real decisions involve limited budgets and competing priorities, which makes them more realistic and less inclined to simply complain. A student representative who helps to design a recycling scheme, for example, learns to present a proposal, gather support and manage a small project.

Furthermore, student involvement improves decisions and school life. Pupils understand daily problems, such as overcrowded corridors, bullying in unsupervised areas or irrelevant lessons, better than adults who are not present, so their suggestions can lead to practical solutions. When students feel heard, they also develop a stronger sense of belonging and are more likely to respect the rules they helped to shape. Nevertheless, involvement must have limits. Matters such as safeguarding, staff appointments and the core curriculum require professional expertise and legal responsibility, so adults should keep the final say. Student voice works best as consultation and shared decision-making on appropriate issues, with clear explanations whenever a suggestion cannot be accepted.

In conclusion, students should be involved in school governance to a large extent, because it builds responsibility and produces better decisions, provided that adults retain authority over professional matters.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that school is a place for students to discover passions rather than focus on exams?

versions.text:
Many pupils feel that school is mainly about preparing for exams. I largely agree that it should instead be a place where students discover their passions, since interest drives learning and careers, although examinations still have an important role.

To begin with, discovering a passion motivates pupils to learn. Students who find that they love programming, music or biology study longer, ask more questions and persevere through difficulties without being pushed, because the work itself is rewarding. Passion also guides choices about future study and careers, so young people who have explored their interests are more likely to find satisfying work. Schools that offer clubs, projects and a wide range of subjects give pupils the opportunity to try many things. A pupil who joins a robotics club and discovers a talent for engineering, for instance, may choose a university course that suits her.

Furthermore, an exclusive focus on exams narrows education and increases stress. Written tests mainly reward memory and speed under timed conditions, while creativity and practical skills go unmeasured, and teaching tends to drift towards test preparation instead of genuine understanding. High-stakes tests also place students under excessive pressure. Admittedly, exams cannot be abandoned: qualifications are needed for university and employment, and they provide a fair standard. The aim should be balance, with exam preparation taking its place alongside exploration rather than dominating every lesson.

In conclusion, school should be mainly a place to discover passions, because this motivates learning and guides careers, as long as examinations keep a sensible but limited role.

essays.question: What are the causes of teacher burnout? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
The issue of teacher burnout is a growing concern in many countries. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Heavy workloads combined with modest pay are a significant source of teacher burnout. Teachers who face long hours, endless paperwork and relatively low salaries often feel undervalued and exhausted, and many either leave the profession or never enter it. In addition, constant pressure from inspections, test targets and large, sometimes difficult classes leaves little room for recovery, and many teachers receive little emotional support. A teacher who marks papers every evening and weekend, for example, has almost no time to rest, so exhaustion accumulates over the years. This vicious circle leaves the remaining staff with even more to handle.

To address this issue, stronger support systems would reduce the strain on teachers. Counselling services, mentoring schemes and reasonable limits on workload ensure that problems are identified early instead of escalating into crises. In addition, governments should commit more funding to schools, since this tackles the problem at its source. Extra money can be channelled into hiring teaching assistants, reducing class sizes and cutting unnecessary paperwork, which relieves pressure where it is felt most. Fair salaries and clear career pathways would also make teaching a respected and sustainable profession. Prevention of this kind is far less costly than dealing with the consequences later, because experienced teachers who stay are worth far more than constant replacements.

In conclusion, teacher burnout stems mainly from heavy workloads and lack of support, but stronger support systems and greater investment offer a realistic way forward.

essays.question: Many people think that podcasting is a powerful educational tool. Do you agree? Explain with examples.

versions.text:
Podcasts, audio programmes that can be downloaded and played anywhere, have become popular far beyond entertainment. I agree that they are a powerful educational tool, since they make learning accessible and engaging, although they work best as a supplement to other methods.

To begin with, podcasts allow people to learn at times and in places where reading or watching is impossible. Learners can listen on the way to work, while exercising or doing housework, so time that would otherwise be wasted becomes study time. Lessons can be paused, replayed and played at different speeds, which helps students who need to hear an explanation more than once. Audio is also valuable for people with visual impairments and for those who learn best by listening. A commuter who spends an hour on the train each day, for example, can work through a whole language course in a few months.

Furthermore, a good podcast engages listeners through stories, interviews and expert voices. Hearing a historian describe an event or a scientist explain a discovery makes a subject feel alive in a way that a textbook paragraph often cannot, and language learners benefit from regular exposure to natural speech, accents and vocabulary. Most podcasts are also free or inexpensive, which widens access. However, listening is a passive activity, and without exercises, discussion or feedback, listeners may forget much of what they hear. Podcasts should therefore be combined with activities that require learners to respond.

In conclusion, I believe that podcasts are a powerful educational tool because they are flexible, accessible and engaging, provided that they are used alongside interactive learning.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on lifelong learning programs? Use examples.

versions.text:
Rapid technological change means that few people can rely on a single set of skills for an entire career. This essay will outline two key benefits for a country that focuses on lifelong learning programmes: a more adaptable workforce and a healthier, more inclusive society.

First and foremost, lifelong learning keeps the workforce adaptable. Workers must update their knowledge regularly to stay employable, and programmes that provide affordable evening courses and short online training allow them to move into new roles when old ones disappear. As a result, unemployment is lower, companies find the skills they need and productivity rises. A factory worker whose job is automated, for example, can retrain as a technician and remain in work instead of relying on benefits. A country that invests in such programmes is therefore better able to cope with economic change.

In addition, lifelong learning improves wellbeing and social inclusion. Adults who return to education gain confidence, make friends and keep their minds active, which can reduce isolation and support healthy ageing. It also offers a second chance to those who left school early or could not afford university, narrowing the gap between rich and poor and strengthening social mobility. Learners who value education tend to encourage their children to study, so the benefits pass to the next generation. Furthermore, better-educated citizens are more inclined to make healthier choices, which eases the burden on healthcare services and frees public money for other priorities.

To sum up, lifelong learning programmes bring clear benefits to a country, above all an adaptable workforce and a more inclusive, healthier society. For these reasons, they deserve sustained public support.

essays.question: What are the causes of overcrowded classrooms? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
The issue of overcrowded classrooms is a growing concern in many countries. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Chronic underfunding is a major contributor to overcrowded classrooms. When budgets are tight, schools cannot recruit enough qualified staff, maintain their buildings or construct new ones, so existing classes simply grow larger. The resulting strain on existing resources makes the situation steadily worse. In addition, rapid population growth and urban migration contribute to this problem. When families move to cities faster than new schools are built, existing classrooms must absorb additional children. Over time, this pushes class sizes well beyond a manageable level. A city school built for six hundred pupils that now enrols nine hundred, for example, must squeeze three children into spaces designed for two.

To address this issue, governments should commit more funding to education, since this tackles the problem at its source. Extra money can be channelled into recruiting teachers, constructing classrooms and modernising equipment, which relieves pressure where it is felt most. School building should also be planned in line with population data, so that authorities that track migration can build schools and recruit teachers in advance. In addition, authorities should offer attractive incentives such as higher salaries and housing support to attract teachers to overcrowded districts. Temporary measures such as shift systems and online lessons can relieve pressure while new classrooms are built, although they should not become permanent.

In conclusion, overcrowded classrooms stem mainly from underfunding and rapid population growth, but greater investment and careful planning offer a realistic way forward.

essays.question: To what extent should cultural diversity be promoted in schools? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
Modern classrooms often include children from many cultural backgrounds. I largely agree that schools should actively promote cultural diversity, since it reduces prejudice and helps every pupil to feel valued, although it must be done sincerely rather than symbolically.

To begin with, promoting diversity broadens pupils' horizons and weakens prejudice. When schools celebrate different languages, festivals and histories, children learn to appreciate traditions other than their own, and they are less likely to rely on stereotypes. In a globalised world, this understanding is also a practical skill, since graduates are likely to work with colleagues and clients from many countries, which gives them a clear advantage in a competitive labour market. A school that invites parents to share cooking and stories from their home countries, for example, helps pupils to see differences as interesting instead of threatening.

Furthermore, recognising diversity helps minority pupils to feel that they belong. Children who see their language, religion and history respected in the curriculum are more confident and engaged, which improves attendance and results, whereas those who feel invisible may withdraw or face bullying. A sense of belonging also strengthens cooperation across groups. However, the promotion of diversity should not be tokenistic, such as a single international day each year. It needs to be reflected in teaching materials, staff training and everyday practice, and it must emphasise shared values alongside differences so that all pupils feel part of one community.

In conclusion, schools should promote cultural diversity to a large extent because it builds understanding and belonging, provided that the effort is genuine and consistent.

essays.question: Discuss the role of tutors in supplementing education.

versions.text:
Private tuition has become a common supplement to formal schooling. This essay will outline two roles that tutors play in supplementing education: providing individual attention, and building confidence and examination skills.

First and foremost, tutors give each learner individual attention. In a crowded classroom, a teacher rarely has time to adjust the pace for every pupil, whereas a tutor can identify a student's weaknesses and provide targeted practice at once. Consequently, gaps in knowledge are closed before they grow, and quicker learners are stretched with more advanced material. Because a tutor can focus on one pupil, explanations can be repeated in several ways until the idea is clear. A pupil who repeatedly makes the same mathematical error, for instance, can receive tailored exercises the same day instead of waiting weeks for feedback.

In addition, tutors build confidence and prepare students for examinations. A patient adult who explains a topic without classmates watching helps hesitant pupils to ask questions and to believe in their ability. Tutors also teach revision techniques and exam skills, which can reduce anxiety and improve results. However, private tuition has drawbacks. It is expensive, so wealthy families enjoy a clear advantage over equally able classmates, and heavy reliance on tutors may leave pupils dependent on outside help. Governments and schools can reduce this inequality by offering free tutoring schemes and after-school support for disadvantaged pupils, so that the benefits are shared more widely.

To sum up, tutors play a valuable role in education by giving individual attention and building confidence, provided that access is made fairer.

essays.question: Some believe that art education should be prioritized over competitive sports. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Budgets and timetables are limited, so some people argue that art education deserves priority over competitive sports. I disagree with this view, since both contribute to children's development, and competitive sport offers health benefits and lessons in resilience that art alone cannot provide.

To begin with, sport contributes to physical health, which is increasingly urgent. Many children now spend hours sitting at screens, and rates of obesity and related illness are rising in many countries. Regular sport keeps pupils active, builds fitness and establishes habits that can last for life, whereas art lessons, however valuable, do not exercise the body. Schools that reduce sport to make room for art may therefore damage health and increase pressure on health services in the future. A child who plays football three times a week, for example, is more likely to stay active as an adult.

Furthermore, competitive sport teaches qualities that are difficult to develop elsewhere. Pupils learn to cooperate with teammates, take responsibility for the group and cope with both winning and losing, which builds resilience and self-control. Training also teaches discipline, since improvement comes from patient, repeated effort. Admittedly, art develops creativity and emotional expression, and some children thrive in studios more than on playing fields. For this reason, the two should not be set against each other. A balanced school gives every pupil access to both, and neither should be sacrificed to the other.

In conclusion, I do not believe that art education should be prioritised over competitive sport, because each develops different strengths that children need, and a balanced timetable serves them best.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on public safety education? Use examples.

versions.text:
Safety education ranges from road awareness to first aid and emergency preparedness. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that teaches public safety in schools: fewer deaths and injuries, and stronger, more resilient communities.

First and foremost, safety education saves lives and prevents injuries. Children who learn how to cross roads, swim safely, recognise fire hazards and perform basic first aid are better able to protect themselves and others, and these skills last for life. Accidents are a major cause of death and injury among young people, so even modest improvements in awareness can have a large effect. As a result, hospitals treat fewer preventable injuries, and families are spared tragedy. A pupil who knows how to give first aid, for example, may be able to help a classmate who is choking before an ambulance arrives.

In addition, safety education builds resilient and responsible communities. Pupils who practise emergency drills and learn what to do in earthquakes, floods or fires respond calmly instead of panicking, which reduces damage and the burden on emergency services. Beyond personal advancement, such education brings wider benefits to society as a whole, because children carry the knowledge home and share it with parents and neighbours. Lessons on online safety and road behaviour also encourage a sense of shared responsibility. Preparing people in advance is far cheaper than dealing with disasters after they occur, so governments that invest in safety education save public money as well as lives.

To sum up, public safety education brings clear benefits to a country, above all fewer preventable deaths and more resilient communities. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.
